clue.text: Nothing to pick up from speech

parts.note: nothing is zero, which looks like the letter O
to rally is to recover or pick up after a setback

explanation.surface: Someone finds there is nothing worth gleaning from a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Something conveyed by spoken word rather than writing is delivered in that manner, so 'from speech' works as an adverb.

clue.text: Resort hotel used by most after refurbishment

indicators.note: a refurbished building has been rearranged and done up, so the letters of 'most' are reordered

parts.note: the Ritz is a famous luxury hotel name

explanation.surface: Most guests stay at a resort hotel once it has been done up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used by' is a link: the rearranged letters of 'most' come before the hotel's name. 'Resort' looks like a verb but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: St Moritz is a famous Swiss ski resort and spa town.

clue.text: It's futile to rob, when willing to go without

indicators.note: to go without, i.e. outside, means the word for 'when' wraps around the piece for 'rob'

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
to mug someone is to rob them in the street
game means willing, as in 'I'm game'

explanation.surface: A would-be thief decides robbery is pointless when people willingly do without.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go without' reads as abstaining, but it means AS goes outside MUG.
explanation.definitionFit: Something called a mug's game is an activity only a fool would pursue, being pointless or unrewarding.

clue.text: Old letter, however near, sent back

parts.note: tho is a short informal form of though, meaning however

indicators.note: something sent back goes the other way, so the abbreviation for near is reversed

explanation.surface: An old letter is returned to sender, though from someone nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorn was an Old English runic character representing the th sound, so it is an archaic letter.

clue.text: Lass holds a very colourful gemstone

indicators.note: one word holding another contains it within its letters

parts.note: a lass is a girl
so means very, as in 'so good'

explanation.surface: A young woman clutches a brilliantly coloured jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very' looks like part of the description of the gem, but it is wordplay giving SO.
explanation.definitionFit: A girasol is a fire opal, a gem that shows bright flashes of colour.

clue.text: Corporation needing rating to satisfy people

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a naval rating
to do can mean to suffice or satisfy, as in 'that will do'
men stands for people in general

explanation.surface: A company needs a credit rating to keep its customers happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' is the jocular word for a pot belly, not a business.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation is an old humorous term for a large paunch, so it names the belly.

clue.text: Celebrity's ringed one? That should be "rung"

indicators.note: ringed means circled, so the celebrity word surrounds the figure one

parts.note: a celebrity is a star
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A grammarian corrects 'ringed' to 'rung' while discussing a celebrity's phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'ringed'/'rung' as grammar, but rung means a step, and a stair is one.
explanation.definitionFit: A rung is one step of a ladder, and a single step in a staircase is a stair.

clue.text: After rejection at last, I express great disappointment?

indicators.note: at last picks out the final letter of 'rejection'

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to vent is to express feelings openly

explanation.surface: Having been turned down, someone voices their deep disappointment.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-event is a much-hyped occasion that turns out to be a letdown or anticlimax.

clue.text: Hard to cut beef? Hamburger's my sort of food!

indicators.note: to cut into something is to go inside it, so H goes into the bovine word

parts.note: beef cattle are cows, so beef suggests cow
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
a person from Hamburg would say mein for my in German

explanation.surface: Tough beef is hard to slice, but someone loves a hamburger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamburger' is a native of Hamburg, not a burger.
explanation.definitionFit: Chow mein is a Chinese dish of fried noodles, a type of food.

clue.text: National opera company's ignored on return

indicators.note: on return means the remaining letters are read backwards
ignored means left out, so the company abbreviation is dropped

parts.note: Nabucco is Verdi's opera
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A national opera company is snubbed when it comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' removes the company abbreviation from Verdi's opera, leaving NABUC, and 'on return' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A national of Cuba, one of its citizens, is called this.

clue.text: Pal of an eccentric Scottish sandwich maker

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A friend of an oddball Scot makes sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: A pan loaf is the Scottish name for a loaf baked in a tin, from which sandwiches are made.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is what a sandwich is made from, and this is a Scots term for a tin-baked loaf.

clue.text: Country, once submerged in propaganda, is surprisingly backward

indicators.note: backward means the letters are taken from right to left
submerged in means sitting below the surface of these words, inside them

explanation.surface: A former state is found to be lagging, according to its own propaganda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' looks like an anagram signal but is part of the letter run.
explanation.definitionFit: Prussia was a German kingdom and state that no longer exists, so a former country.

clue.text: Dodges customs after tip from officer

indicators.note: after puts the customs word behind the tip letter
tip means the end point of 'officer', its final letter

parts.note: uses are customs or habitual practices

explanation.surface: Someone evades customs checks after a word from an officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruses are tricks or stratagems, and dodges is a noun for such tricks.

clue.text: Made tart turn to God briefly? I had one about to turn

indicators.note: to turn means everything before it is read backwards
briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to deify is to make into a god
I'd is the contraction of I had
one is the Roman numeral I
CA, circa, means about

explanation.surface: A woman of loose morals turns to religion, having been converted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' reverses DEIF, ID, I and CA together, reading DEIFIDICA backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To acidify something is to make it sour, and tart means sour.

clue.text: Graves could be on this land — stone where prophet's buried

parts.note: to land a prize is to win it
Eli is a biblical prophet and priest
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

explanation.surface: Graves might be dug in the land under a stone marking a prophet's burial.
explanation.walkthrough: Graves is a Bordeaux wine, not burial plots.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant's list of wines on offer might include a bottle of Graves, the Bordeaux red or white.

clue.text: Key needed to open a precious metal antique?

indicators.note: opening up a word lets another go inside, so the key letter goes inside the metal

parts.note: gold is a precious metal
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A key is required to unlock a safe of old gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Something age-old has existed for a very long time, as an antique has.

clue.text: Men by hospital holding signal up, almost turning amber?

indicators.note: holding means the men and hospital letters enclose the next part

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers or men

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: signal is taken as it stands before trimming

explanation.surface: Soldiers at a hospital wait as the traffic signal nearly changes to amber.
explanation.walkthrough: SIGNAL cut by 'almost' gives SIGNA, which 'up' reverses to ANGIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something becoming amber is taking on a somewhat orange colour.

clue.text: Tanks answer as artillery surrounds one

parts.note: qua is Latin for as, in the capacity of

indicators.note: surrounds means the artillery letters go round one

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Tanks respond as the artillery closes round a target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tanks' suggests armour, but these are fish tanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquaria are glass tanks in which fish and water creatures are kept.

clue.text: Back-breaking stress carries on over time, untreated

parts.note: lasts means carries on or continues
raw means untreated or unprocessed

explanation.surface: Back pain from stress persists over time without treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to the straw that broke the camel's back.
explanation.definitionFit: The final burden that makes something unbearable, from the proverb of the camel's breaking back.

clue.text: A number of Galician cats and dogs?

definitions.text: A number of Galician cats and dogs?

parts.words: A number of Galician cats and dogs?
parts.note: a number is a song, here from My Fair Lady; Galicia is in Spain and raining cats and dogs is a downpour

explanation.walkthrough: 'number' means a song: the line from My Fair Lady about Spanish weather.
explanation.definitionFit: This My Fair Lady song names rainfall in a Spanish setting, as Galicia in north-west Spain is.

clue.text: Did plump, round boy set about training?

indicators.note: set about means placed around, so round and boy letters enclose the training abbreviation

parts.note: O is round in shape
Ed is a boy's name
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: A chubby lad began exercising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plump' looks like an adjective for the boy but is the verb, as in plump for.
explanation.definitionFit: To plump for something is to choose it, so did plump means chose.

clue.text: Press staff to institute endurance event

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
to man a post is to staff it

explanation.surface: The newspaper staff set up a gruelling athletic event.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ironman is a long-distance triathlon, a severe test of stamina.

clue.text: Energy saving paid for by dividing into regions

indicators.note: saving means keeping inside, so the energy word holds the next piece

parts.note: zing means energy or zest
on means paid for by, as in 'drinks are on me'

explanation.surface: Energy-saving measures are funded by splitting the country into areas.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoning is the planning practice of dividing land into areas for set uses.

clue.text: Rashly offer new deal: alas, to be ignored

indicators.note: rashly means recklessly, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A rash new offer goes unheeded, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that fall on deaf ears are disregarded by listeners.

clue.text: Break, more than once, posh sort of vase cleaning

parts.note: vac is short for vacation, a break

indicators.note: more than once means the posh letter appears twice

parts.note: U means upper-class or posh
a Ming vase is from the Chinese Ming dynasty

explanation.surface: Someone keeps breaking a posh vase while doing housework.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoovering is a method of cleaning floors with a suction machine.

clue.text: Opened sandwiches container that's not open

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between, so the opened word encloses the container

parts.note: undid means opened, as a parcel
a can is a container

explanation.surface: Someone opened a lunchbox holding sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uncandid is not frank or forthcoming in what they say.

clue.text: Offer youth such training?

parts.note: to hand someone something is to offer it
a son is a youth or lad

explanation.surface: A parent proposes some practical training for a young man.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition relies on 'such' pointing back: practical training is the kind described.
explanation.definitionFit: Practical, learning-by-doing instruction is described with this term.

clue.text: Code nearly broken revealed the lot?

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: bust means broken
hid nothing, with O as zero, is a jokey way of saying revealed everything

explanation.surface: A secret code, almost cracked, gave away everything.
explanation.walkthrough: The query flags that 'revealed the lot' is read as HID O, hid nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushido is the samurai code of honour and conduct in Japan.

clue.text: Get higher certificates for films — series

parts.note: U, universal, is a film classification
PG, parental guidance, is another film classification
a row is a series or line

explanation.surface: Movies in a series earn higher ratings.
explanation.walkthrough: U and PG are British film age ratings.
explanation.definitionFit: To upgrow is an archaic verb meaning to grow up or become taller.

clue.text: Diver, topless, put up with looks at first

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: to house someone is to put them up

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of 'looks'

explanation.surface: A topless diver tolerates being looked at.
explanation.walkthrough: The ousel or water ouzel is the dipper, a bird that dives into streams.
explanation.definitionFit: The water ousel, or dipper, is a songbird that dives underwater to feed.
